items.title: When Beauvoir's Le Deuxieme Sexe appeared
items.claim: Simone de Beauvoir's Le Deuxieme Sexe was published in which year?
items.reveal:
The book contains the often-cited line 'On ne nait pas femme: on le devient' ('One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman').

The Vatican placed it on the Index of Forbidden Books in 1956.
items.why: A single publication can crystallise a long intellectual movement and trigger immediate institutional reaction.

items.title: France and minority languages
items.claim: Which European Charter for Regional or Minority Languages instrument has France signed but not yet ratified?

options.text: France signed in 1999 but has not ratified, citing constitutional issues

items.reveal:
The 1958 Constitution's Article 2 declares 'la langue de la Republique est le francais', cited as an obstacle to ratification.

A 2021 law strengthening regional language teaching was partially overturned by the Constitutional Council.
items.why: Constitutional commitments to a single official language can constrain participation in international minority-language frameworks.

items.title: Where most French speakers will live
items.claim: OIF (Observatoire de la langue francaise) projections suggest that by 2050, roughly what share of French speakers will live in Africa?
items.reveal_title: Most French speakers will be African
items.reveal:
OIF estimates (Demographie et langue francaise reports) project that demographic growth in francophone Africa will lift the African share of French speakers to around 85% by 2050.

This follows from population growth in countries such as DR Congo, where French is an official or working language.
items.why: The geographic centre of a language can shift dramatically across a generation.
